analysis.investment_thesis: Borosil Renewables fails both Magic Formula tests decisively: Earnings Yield of ~0.8% (EBIT ₹58 Cr / EV ~₹7,186 Cr) is near-zero, and ROIC of ~5.3% (EBIT / capital employed of ~₹1,092 Cr) is well below the 20% threshold for a quality business. This is an expensive, capital-intensive, loss-making manufacturer with no near-term Magic Formula merit.
key_strengths: India's only domestic solar glass manufacturer — structural import-substitution positioning
Revenue doubled from ₹642 Cr (FY2022) to ₹1,476 Cr (FY2025), showing real demand growth
Low D/E of 0.23 and borrowings down sharply to ₹203 Cr in FY2025 after peaking at ₹576 Cr
key_risks: Severe margin collapse: operating income plunged from ₹223 Cr (FY2022) to ₹58 Cr (FY2025) as revenue nearly doubled — cost structure deeply broken
Persistent free cash flow destruction: FCF negative in 4 of last 5 years, cumulative capex of ₹1,047 Cr since FY2022 with no earnings to show for it
Chinese solar glass dumping risk — Chinese producers have crushed global solar glass prices, directly threatening Borosil's margins and business model
red_flags: Net profit negative for two consecutive years: -₹50 Cr (FY2024), -₹87 Cr (FY2025) — worsening losses
ROE -8.9% and ROCE -4.41%: destroying shareholder capital, not creating it
Earnings Yield of ~0.8% on EV of ₹7,186 Cr — stock priced for perfection despite operational deterioration
Operating income collapsed 74% (₹223 Cr → ₹58 Cr) even as revenue grew 130% — catastrophic operating leverage in reverse
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math is damning. EBIT stands at ₹58 Cr on an Enterprise Value of ~₹7,186 Cr (market cap ₹6,987 Cr + net debt ₹199 Cr), yielding an Earnings Yield of just 0.81% — against my 12% threshold. Return on Capital (EBIT ÷ capital employed of ~₹1,092 Cr) is ~5.3%, far below the 20% minimum. A P/E of 73x (on whatever normalized earnings basis the market is using) and EV/EBITDA of 20x for a business earning negative net returns is speculation, not investing. This stock ranks in the bottom decile on both Magic Formula dimensions simultaneously.

The business narrative is sympathetic — India needs domestic solar glass and Borosil is the sole local producer. But the economics have deteriorated sharply: operating margins collapsed from 34% in FY2022 to just 4% in FY2025, almost certainly due to Chinese price pressure. The company has deployed ₹1,047 Cr in capex over three years and generated cumulatively negative free cash flow. Until Chinese anti-dumping duties provide real relief and ROIC sustainably exceeds cost of capital, the Magic Formula demands we pass entirely.
